name_reason: Current name 'runtime_battle_state' is a misnomer. The symbol is a base pointer to FDOTHER.DAT resource index 1, a packed 24x24 sprite atlas (offset table at +6, per-tile 4-byte absolute offsets), used purely as a cursor/highlight sprite sheet. Loaded by main @ 0x25BF4 via fd2_load_dat_resource(FDOTHER.DAT, ptr, 1) -- the exact same free-then-reload pattern and access pattern as its sibling FDOTHER sprite-sheet pointers (data_fd2_chinese_font_sheet idx4, data_fd2_ui_anim_sprite_sheet_ptr idx5, data_fd2_resource_portrait_sheet_ptr idx6). All 3 readers treat it as a sprite-sheet base: fd2_blit_24x24_at_window_relative_pos @ 0x12779 (tile_idx=caller arg), fd2_render_recruitment_select_screen @ 0x31F27 (tile 0 = cursor highlight), fd2_render_battle_scene_with_portrait_grid_layout @ 0x3412C (tile 0 = reserved-position highlight overlay). No battle-state semantics whatsoever. Proposed name follows the data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention with the _sheet_ptr descriptor matching its siblings and reflecting the pointer-to-sprite-sheet data type. No address residue in proposed name.
purpose: Base pointer to the cursor/highlight 24x24 sprite atlas (FDOTHER.DAT resource index 1), loaded once at startup and read by 3 UI/menu render routines.
logic_summary: main @ 0x25BF4 assigns ptr = fd2_load_dat_resource(FDOTHER.DAT, ptr, 1), passing the prior value (NULL on first call) so the loader frees-then-reloads. The resource buffer is a packed sprite atlas: header byte +6 onward is a table of 4-byte absolute byte-offsets, one per tile index; the RLE pixel stream for tile N is at base + *(int32*)(base + 6 + N*4). The 3 readers blit a 24x24 tile from this atlas: fd2_blit_24x24_at_window_relative_pos uses a caller-supplied tile index (battle-window cursor sprites); the two render-screen functions use tile index 0 as the cursor / reserved-position highlight overlay.
datatype: uint32 (4-byte address slot / resource pointer). Ghidra data type at 0x53A4D is 'undefined' len=1, but every access is 32-bit (PUSH/MOV dword ptr [0x53a4d]); src declares uint32. The decompiler's '_data_fd2_runtime_battle_state_ptr overlaps smaller symbols' warning is a cosmetic artifact of the 4-byte synthetic view over the 1-byte undefined data, not a real layout issue.
element_semantics: Holds the malloc'd resource buffer base address returned by fd2_load_dat_resource. The pointed-to buffer is a packed sprite atlas: bytes [0..5] header, then at +6 a per-tile table of 4-byte absolute byte-offsets; each entry resolves to that tile's RLE-encoded 24x24 pixel stream within the same buffer.
comment_original_issue: Original src comment described it as 'base pointer of the runtime battle/cursor state block', which mischaracterizes the content. It is a sprite atlas (sprite sheet), not a state block, and has no battle-state role; it is a sibling of the other FDOTHER sprite-sheet pointers.
